For repeated whole H=C^d, the necessary/sufficient constraint Σv_i²(S_i−I)=0 and positive definiteness are exact; solve one matrix from the others, giving real dimension (m−1)d² and a realizable open convex region by taking frames S_i^{1/2}e_j. These are exact operator calculations, not verifier claims.

value.rationale: Correcting a false theorem about distributed fusion-frame processing protects inference from aggregate global frame operators to local Parsevalness, where redundant systems are a principal use case. A minimal exact counterexample, correct compression criterion and full repeated-block classification provide a reusable structural insight, not merely a cheap zero-check.

final_claim: Equality of fusion and global frame operators means the compression P_R(⊕(I−S_i))|_R vanishes, not the whole defect on R. A two-block one-dimensional non-Parseval example contradicts Köhldorfer–Balazs Corollary 4.12(1); repeated full-space blocks admit a dimension (m−1)d² open convex family of cancelling positive local frame operators.
limitations: Refutes only the unqualified claim in part (1); fusion Riesz bases and appropriate one-sided conditions remain valid.
The (m−1)d² dimension counts local self-adjoint frame operators, not individual frame vector parameterizations.
